draft.shortGloss: to choose; to vote; to dial
draft.emotion: thoughtful and deliberate, taking a moment to consider the options
notes: For everyday picking out of items (like a gift or clothes), 'aussuchen' is more common; 'wählen' sounds slightly more formal or is used for options on a menu or list.
Unlike English 'vote for', 'wählen' takes a direct accusative object without a preposition: 'wen wählst du?' (who are you voting for?).

senses.definition: To decide which option you want from several possibilities.

examples.text: Sie können zwischen zwei Gerichten wählen.
examples.translation: You can choose between two dishes.

senses.definition: To cast a ballot for a candidate or party in an election.

examples.text: Die Bürger wählen am Sonntag einen neuen Bürgermeister.
examples.translation: The citizens will vote for a new mayor on Sunday.
examples.emotion: serious and civic-minded, describing a public process

senses.definition: To enter a telephone number in order to make a call.

examples.text: Bei einem Notfall musst du die 112 wählen.
examples.translation: In an emergency, you have to dial 112.

draftBefore.shortGloss: to choose; to select; to vote
draftBefore.emotion: thoughtful and deliberate, taking a moment to consider the options
notes: Use 'wählen' when you are picking something out of a set of options (like choosing a meal or a candidate).
It is also the standard verb for 'voting' in an election.

senses.definition: To decide which one you want from several possibilities.

examples.text: Du kannst dir ein Geschenk wählen.
